clue.text: Decline to have a nap

blocks.note: first meaning: to fall away or lessen
second meaning: to fall asleep briefly

explanation.surface: Someone declining an invitation in order to take a nap instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline to' reads as refusing to do something; here it is a separate verb meaning to dwindle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both a falling away in numbers and nodding off into sleep.

clue.text: Its root goes into a stew

definitions.text: Its root goes into a stew

indicators.note: to stew is to cook things down into a jumbled mass, so the preceding letters get mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook drops a root vegetable into a simmering pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: rice, its root ingredient, is cooked down into a stew-like dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian rice dish is simmered slowly in stock, much like a thick stew of grains.

clue.text: Pakistani opener does badly and gets stumped

indicators.note: an opener is whoever goes first, so only the first letter of the word is kept
doing something badly means doing it wrong, so the letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: the first letter of Pakistani
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Pakistani opening batsman plays poorly and is stumped by the wicketkeeper in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Stumped is a way of being out in cricket, which the surface leans on; here it means baffled. To pose someone is to puzzle them with a hard question.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone posed has been set a baffling question, left puzzled and unable to answer, just as stumped means.

clue.text: Drop in radio activity?

blocks.note: surface reading: a dip in broadcasting, perhaps fewer listeners tuning in
setter's reading: say it as radioactivity, and the drop is particles falling to earth after a nuclear blast

explanation.walkthrough: Splitting radioactivity into two words disguises the nuclear sense as broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Radioactive particles descend from the atmosphere after an explosion, literally dropping down as contaminated dust.

clue.text: Point to observe about international runner

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is placed around the other here

blocks.note: a compass point: east
to observe is to see
a cap is awarded for each international match a player appears in, so an international is a cap

explanation.surface: Pointing out a sprinter who competes for their country.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport an international player is called a cap, after the cap awarded for each appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner can be someone who has fled or absconded, and an escapee is exactly that fugitive.

clue.text: Employees used to keep up standards

blocks.note: first meaning: workforces
second meaning: poles that hold flags aloft

explanation.surface: Workers are relied on to maintain quality in an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standards' looks like quality levels, but it means flags, which are held up on poles.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means bodies of workers and also the poles or rods on which banners and flags are raised.

clue.text: The supporters present in the new stand

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh order
one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Fans are gathered in a newly built grandstand.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents are followers who stick to a cause or team, so they are its backers and loyal fans.

clue.text: Characteristic note on organ

indicators.note: in a down answer, one thing on another sits beneath it, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
to note something is to mark it, and a mark is a written note

explanation.surface: A distinctive sound played on a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' and 'organ' suggest music; here the organ is a body part. Earmark comes from the tags cut into livestock ears.
explanation.definitionFit: An earmark is an identifying trait or distinguishing feature, just as a characteristic marks something out.

clue.text: Man in comic duo sadly out of touch

indicators.note: things going sadly have gone wrong, so the letters end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: One half of a comedy double act has sadly lost contact with the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Incommunicado means unreachable and cut off from communication, which is being unable to be contacted.

clue.text: Requests time off from jobs

indicators.note: taking something off from another removes it, so one letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
jobs are tasks

explanation.surface: An employee asks for leave from work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests asking for time off work; instead T is removed from the front of TASKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for putting forward a demand or plea, so someone who requests something asks for it.

clue.text: Charles I wandering round an English county

indicators.note: a wandering thing strays from its path, so these letters stray from their order
going round something means surrounding it, so the jumbled letters enclose a short word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Stuart king Charles I travels around one of England's counties.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'an' does double duty: it goes inside the jumbled letters and also reads as part of the definition. LANCASHIRE is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is one of the historic shire regions of north-west England, home to Manchester and Liverpool historically.

clue.text: The artist's sitting-room

blocks.note: surface reading: the lounge in a painter's house
setter's reading: the room where a model sits for a portrait

explanation.walkthrough: Sitting-room normally means a lounge; here it is a room for sittings, the sessions in which a subject poses.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters and photographers work in this workroom, where clients sit to have their portraits made.

clue.text: Out to the opening ball from a spin bowler

blocks.note: out, as in switched off or gone off
an opening or gap is a break

explanation.surface: A batsman is out to the very first ball, delivered by a spinner.
explanation.walkthrough: An OFF-BREAK is a cricket delivery from a finger-spinner that turns from the off side towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a delivery in cricket bowled by a slow spinner, so it is one kind of ball such a bowler sends down.

clue.text: Doctors mention it too late

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Physicians raise a diagnosis only when it is already too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' reads as a plural noun for physicians, but it is a verb meaning tampers with.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving after the deadline or proper moment is the same as missing the due hour or being overdue.

clue.text: I'm to intercede without delay

blocks.note: taken as written
to intercede between parties is to mediate

explanation.surface: Someone announces that they are about to step in to settle a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at once, instantly and promptly, happens with no pause, which is what the adjective conveys.

clue.text: A poisonous creeper

blocks.note: surface reading: a toxic climbing plant such as poison ivy
setter's reading: an animal that creeps along the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Creeper first suggests a vine; here it is a creature that slithers.
explanation.definitionFit: Many species of this legless reptile are venomous and move by sliding along close to the ground.

clue.text: French ill-translated by doctor in Sweden

blocks.note: mal is the French word for ill or bad
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A French phrase about illness is badly rendered by a physician in Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: MALMO is a city in southern Sweden; the definition names only where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmo is a major port city on the southern tip of Sweden, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Normally Laura's out with sweetheart

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are scrambled
the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
the middle letter of sweet

explanation.surface: Laura usually goes out on a date with her boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' looks like a boyfriend, but it is split: the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually or generally, describing what happens in the ordinary run of things.

clue.text: One doesn't like to show it

definitions.text: One doesn't like to show it

blocks.clueFragment: One doesn't like to show it
blocks.note: surface reading: something a person is reluctant to reveal, such as embarrassment
setter's reading: one who dislikes someone displays this feeling

explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't like to' reads as reluctance; split differently, it is disliking someone, which is shown by hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is strong hostility or ill will, the feeling displayed by someone who dislikes another person.

clue.text: The things they're told are incredible!

definitions.text: The things they're told are incredible!

blocks.clueFragment: The things they're told are incredible!
blocks.note: surface reading: some listeners hear astonishing stories
setter's reading: the soldiers named in the scornful saying about whom you should tell an unbelievable tale

explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'tell that to the marines' scoffs at a story too far-fetched to believe, implying only gullible sea-soldiers would swallow it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names these sea-going soldiers as the audience for tall tales, so they are the ones hearing unbelievable things.

clue.text: Journey to oil rig in North Africa

indicators.note: to rig something is to fix or manipulate it, so these letters are tampered with

blocks.note: a journey is a trip
taken as written

explanation.surface: Travelling out to an oil platform off the coast of North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil rig' reads as one thing, but rig is the instruction acting on oil. TRIPOLI is the capital of Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya, on the Mediterranean coast, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Rent-free

blocks.note: surface reading: living somewhere without paying for lodging
setter's reading: a rent is a tear or rip, and this is free of one

explanation.walkthrough: Rent first suggests payment to a landlord, but it is also a noun for a split in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no rip or tear in it is intact and whole, the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Like one treating Ida with scorn?

definitions.text: Like one treating Ida with scorn?

indicators.note: treating material means processing it into another form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing someone who sneers at a woman called Ida.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: someone mocking Ida would be scornfully mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic means grimly mocking or cynically disdainful, the manner of a person who treats another with contempt.

clue.text: Kick into wind again

blocks.note: first meaning: the jolt of a gun when fired
second meaning: read as ..., to loop round once more

explanation.surface: Kicking a rope or spring so that it winds up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into RE plus coil, so wind is the verb that rhymes with find.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm's backward jerk on firing is its kick, and coiling a rope a second time is rewinding it.

clue.text: There's something hidden here - sounds like money

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the answer is pronounced the same as a word for funds

blocks.note: money is cash

explanation.surface: A secret store found to be full of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a concealed store or hoard, the place where supplies or valuables are kept out of sight.

clue.text: Interpose helpfully to start the crossword

blocks.note: first meaning: to speak up on someone's behalf
second meaning: literally writing the first entry into the grid

explanation.surface: Offering a helpful suggestion to get someone going on their crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual phrase is to put in a good word for someone; the second sense is the literal act of filling in an entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means intervening on another's behalf, and literally means writing an entry into the grid.

clue.text: Unusually cold part of the earth

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are not in their normal order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chilly region of the globe, such as the polar zones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' suggests the planet; here it is soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod is a lump of soil or clay, so it is a piece of the ground's dirt.

clue.text: Puts down clerics without me

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the clerics stand outside the next word

blocks.note: deans are senior clergymen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Church officials are dismissive, leaving the speaker out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking, which would delete ME; here it means outside, so ME goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to belittle or humiliate them, which is what putting someone down means.

clue.text: His view of life is austere, one might say sour

definitions.text: His view of life is austere
definitions.note: the definition is a clause describing a person, while the answer is a noun for that person

indicators.note: saying something means voicing it, so the answer is a word pronounced like the next one

blocks.note: sour like vinegar, whose acid gives it this adjective

explanation.surface: A sour-faced person with a severe, joyless outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic is someone who practises strict self-denial, renouncing comforts for a severely disciplined life.
